references.text: God forbids Noah and his descendants to eat meat with blood in it, establishing the fundamental prohibition against consuming blood.
An eternal statute that prohibits eating fat and blood, and reaffirms the ban on consuming blood.
Repeats the prohibition against eating blood from birds or animals, with the threat of being cut off from the people.
Explains that the blood is the seat of life, and repeats the prohibition against eating blood, with the penalty of being cut off.
God turns His face against the one who sins, using the same expression found in Leviticus 17:10 about setting His face against a sinner.
Uses the same expression that God sets His face against the disobedient as punishment.
Moses repeats the prohibition against eating blood and instructs that the blood be poured out on the ground like water.
Elaborates on the ban against consuming blood, explaining that the blood is the life and must not be eaten.
Repeats the prohibition against eating blood in connection with the firstfruits.
Ezekiel warns against eating meat with blood as one of the sins leading to judgment.
The apostles in Jerusalem require Gentile Christians to abstain from blood, in line with the Old Testament prohibition.
The Apostolic Decree reiterates the ban on blood as binding for Gentile Christians.
Paul reminds believers of the Apostolic Decree, which includes the prohibition against blood for Gentile Christians.
